key_insight: LLMPopSim shows that individually modeled AI agents can be aggregated to approximate real-world community health behaviors, with moderate accuracy across locations and time.
clinical_relevance: The framework could help researchers simulate population responses to public health interventions, but it is not yet precise enough for direct clinical or policy decision-making without further calibration.
method: Built AI agent populations from U.S. Census and CDC data
Trained on Hawaii 2018 data and tested on held-out 2022 cohorts from Hawaii and New York State
Compared simulated vs observed colorectal cancer screening and mammography at the ZCTA level
evidence_signal: Across four state-outcome tests, mean absolute error was 3.5 to 15.0 percentage points and ZCTA-level correlations ranged from 0.26 to 0.69, with notable bias in screening estimates.
watch_item: Performance was weaker in communities with lower observed screening prevalence, highlighting calibration and subgroup-fidelity concerns before real-world use.
paper_title: Evaluating agentic simulation for local public health estimation
